Nulla quoque querela est, ubi et mentis bonitas concordat et facti. Origenes etiam ait: Potest aliquid justum injuste fieri, ut quum eleemosyna datur jactantiæ causa, quod non est sine querela.
paras.en: Moreover, in these few words Zachary and Elizabeth are magnificently commended, and in a shortened word an abounding sense is contained. For so great was their justice that they are shown to have fully borne that yoke of the law which was so heavy that Peter testifies of it that [[Acts 15:10|neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear|nec nos nec patres nostri illud portare potuimus]] (words which convey a particular difficulty in keeping it, not an absolute impossibility); and they were like Josue, of whom we read: [[Jos 11:15|he left not one thing undone of all the commandments|Non præteriit Josue de universis mandatis Domini, ne unum quidem verbum]] of the Lord. Whoever, then, desires to imitate Zachary and his wife, let him fulfil that word of the Apostle: [[Rom 12:17|Providing good things, not only in the sight of God but also in the sight of all men|Providentes bona, non tantum coram Deo, sed coram omnibus hominibus]]. Further, according to Ambrose: When we obey the heavenly commandments, we walk in them; and when we judge rightly, we are seen to hold to the justifications of the Lord. And there is no complaint where goodness of mind and goodness of deed agree. Origen too says: Something just can be done unjustly, as when alms are given for the sake of boasting; which is not *without blame* [*sine querela*, the words of the verse].

paras.t: Et non erat illis filius, id est aliqua proles: filius enim hoc loco non tam sexum quam germen designat, sic quod a filia non distinguitur: secundum quam acceptionem ad patrem refertur. Frequenter autem Dominus subtrahit sobolem etiam justis, ut tota eorum spes, affectio, consolatio et occupatio, in Deo stabiliantur. Eo quod esset Elisabeth sterilis. Hæc est una causa, specialisque ratio ex parte uxoris, quod filium non habebant, quoniam illa ex naturali dispositione exstitit infecunda, etiam tempore juventutis. Alia vero causa subjungitur: et ambo processissent in diebus suis, id est, ad tantum senium devenissent, quod ad prolificandum naturaliter inhabiles exstiterunt. Hinc conceptio Joannis ex parte matris suæ fuit miraculosa seu supernaturalis dupliciter, utpote ex parte sterilitatis et senectutis; ex parte vero patris sui fuit miraculosa simpliciter, quia ob senium ejus. Sic et sanctorum Patriarcharum conjuges steriles fuisse leguntur, ut patet in Genesi de Sara conjuge Abrahæ, Rebecca conjuge Isaac, Rachel uxore Jacob.
paras.en: [[1:7|And they had no son|Et non erat illis filius]], that is, any offspring: for *son* here signifies not so much the sex as the offspring, so that it is not distinguished from *daughter*; in which sense it is said in relation to the father. Now the Lord often withholds offspring even from the just, so that all their hope, affection, consolation and occupation may be set firm in God. [[1:7|for that Elizabeth was barren|Eo quod esset Elisabeth sterilis]]. This is one cause, and a particular reason on the wife's side, why they had no son: because she was by natural disposition unfruitful, even in the time of her youth. Another cause is added: [[1:7|and they both were well advanced in years|et ambo processissent in diebus suis]], that is, they had come to such old age that they were by nature unfit to beget offspring. Hence the conception of John was miraculous or supernatural on his mother's side in two ways, namely by reason of her barrenness and of her old age; but on his father's side it was miraculous in one way only, namely by reason of his old age. So too we read that the wives of the holy Patriarchs were barren, as appears in Genesis of Sara the wife of Abraham[[Gen 11:30||]], Rebecca the wife of Isaac[[Gen 25:21||]], and Rachel the wife of Jacob[[Gen 29:31||]].

paras.t: Factum est autem quum sacerdotio fungeretur Zacharias, id est, actus officii seu ordinis sui sacerdotalis exsequeretur in templo, in ordine vicis suæ, id est hebdomada sua ordinaria, seu contingente ipsum ex ordine quo sacerdotes præfati sibi invicem in officio sacerdotis succedebant, ante Deum, id est in conspectu et præsentia seu beneplacito Dei; vel, Ante Deum, id est in templo ubi Deus specialiter habitavit, quemadmodum scriptum est: Dominus in templo sancto suo;
paras.en: [[1:8|And it came to pass, when he executed the priestly function|Factum est autem quum sacerdotio fungeretur]], namely Zachary, that is, when he was performing in the temple the acts of his priestly office or order, [[1:8|in the order of his course|in ordine vicis suæ]], that is, in his ordinary week, the one that fell to him by the order in which the said priests succeeded one another in the priestly office, [[1:8|before God|ante Deum]], that is, in the sight and presence, or the good pleasure, of God; or, *before God*, that is, in the temple, where God especially dwelt, as it is written: [[Ps 10:5|The Lord is in his holy temple|Dominus in templo sancto suo]].

paras.t: sorte exiit, id est secundum exigentiam sortis suæ, quæ fuit octava, ut patuit. Distributiones enim hebdomadarum, in quibus sæpe ministrabant viginti quatuor sacerdotes in templo, datæ fuerunt per sortes: sicque quivis illorum secundum exigentiam et ordinem sortis suæ exivit, vel domum suæ habitationis, vel locum prope templum, in quo loco se sacerdotalibus vestibus induit. Sacerdotes siquidem isti, hebdomada qua ministrabant in templo, castitati vacabant, nec proprias domos ingrediebantur, sed in domunculis circa templum sitis quæ exedræ vocabantur, cubabant. Ut incensum poneret, ingressus in templum Domini. Incensum pro holocausto accipi solet, puta pro sacrificio quod ad divinæ majestatis honorem totaliter comburebatur, ad figurandum quod rationalis creatura debet se Creatoris sui obsequio totaliter mancipare: quo tamen sacrificio specialiter præfiguratus est status religiosorum, qui se totos divino offerunt cultui, Deoque vovent. Interdum vero pro incenso thymiamatis sumitur.
paras.en: [[1:9|it was his lot|sorte exiit]] [literally 'he went out by lot'; Denis explains both words], that is, according to the requirement of his lot, which was the eighth, as was shown. For the distribution of the weeks in which the twenty-four priests ministered in the temple was made by lot: and so each of them, according to the requirement and order of his lot, went out, either from the house where he lived or from a place near the temple, in which he put on the priestly vestments. For these priests, in the week in which they ministered in the temple, gave themselves to chastity, and did not enter their own houses, but slept in little lodgings about the temple, which were called *exedræ*. [[1:9|to offer incense, going into the temple of the Lord|Ut incensum poneret, ingressus in templum Domini]]. *Incense* is commonly taken for a holocaust, that is, for a sacrifice which was wholly burnt for the honour of the divine majesty, to signify that the rational creature ought to give itself over wholly to the service of its Creator: and by this sacrifice the state of religious was especially prefigured, who offer themselves wholly to the worship of God and bind themselves to Him by vow. But sometimes it is taken for the incense of the *thymiama* [the sweet-smelling compound burnt on the golden altar].

paras.t: Sancti patres Ambrosius et Beda hic sentire videntur, sobrie tamen, non multum assertive, quod Zacharias iste fuerit summus sacerdos seu pontifex, quia incensa ponere intra Sancta sanctorum semel in anno soli licebat pontifici. Unde et Gorra ait, quod ingressus est templum, scilicet primo in Sancta, secundo in Sancta sanctorum, cum thure et sanguine; postea rediit in Sancta ad altare incensi: quod secundum Josephum et omnes Sanctos inde loquentes, fuit in loco templi qui dictus est Sanctum vel Sancta; secundum Augustinum vero fuit intra Sancta sanctorum. Sed quoniam Josephus et ceteri Judæorum pontificia ac sacerdotia describentes, de summo sacerdotio hujus Zachariæ nullam (ut dicitur) faciunt mentionem, alii magis et forte probabilius putant, quod non fuit summus sacerdos, nec Sancta sanctorum intravit, sed Sancta, et incensum quod posuit, est illud quod omni die fiebat in altari incensi. Peracto enim sacrificio in altari holocaustorum, quod erat in atrio ubi ministrabant sacerdotes minores, sacerdos qui ministravit et sacrificavit ibidem, manibus suis ac pedibus primo lotis, sumpsit prunas de altari holocaustorum, intransque primam templi partem quæ dicitur Sancta, cremabat in illa thymiama super altare incensi, et tunc fuit sacrificium consummatum. Per illam namque evaporationem seu thurificationem, designabatur offerentis devotio. Et quoniam sacrificia illa legalia non erant per se Deo accepta, sed ex offerentium devotione et fide, idcirco in præfata incensione fuit sacrificii consummatio jam prætacta. Denique his favere videtur, quod in libro Paralipomenon sacerdotibus loquitur Ezechias: Nolite (inquiens) negligere, filii mei; vos elegit Dominus ut stetis coram eo, et ministretis ei, colatisque eum et cremetis ei incensum. Hoc ergo incensum, quod juniores sacerdotes facere potuerunt, posuit Zacharias, incendendo thymiama per prunas prædictas, et illud incensum ponendo super altare incensi, quod item altare aureum appellatur.
paras.en: The holy fathers Ambrose and Bede seem to hold here, though soberly and without much assertion, that this Zachary was the supreme priest, or high priest, because to place incense within the Holy of holies was lawful for the high priest alone, once in the year[[Ex 30:10||]][[Heb 9:7||]]. Hence Gorran too says that he entered the temple, first into the Holy place and secondly into the Holy of holies, with incense and blood, and afterwards returned into the Holy place to the altar of incense; which, according to Josephus and all the Saints who speak of it, was in the part of the temple called the Holy, or the Sanctuary, though according to Augustine it was within the Holy of holies. But since Josephus and the others who describe the high priesthoods and priesthoods of the Jews make no mention (as is said) of the high priesthood of this Zachary, others think, more commonly and perhaps more probably, that he was not the high priest and did not enter the Holy of holies, but the Holy place, and that the incense he placed was that which was offered every day on the altar of incense[[Ex 30:7||]]. For when the sacrifice had been completed on the altar of holocausts, which was in the court where the lesser priests ministered, the priest who had ministered and sacrificed there, having first washed his hands and feet[[Ex 30:19||]], took live coals from the altar of holocausts[[Lev 16:12||]], and entering the first part of the temple, which is called the Holy, burnt the *thymiama* there upon the altar of incense; and then the sacrifice was completed. For by that rising smoke, or censing, the devotion of the offerer was signified; and since those legal sacrifices were not acceptable to God of themselves, but by reason of the devotion and faith of those who offered them, the completion of the sacrifice, as was said, lay in this burning of incense. Lastly, this seems to be favoured by what Ezechias says to the priests in the book of Paralipomenon: [[2 Par 29:11|My sons, be not negligent: the Lord hath chosen you to stand before him, and to minister to him, and to worship him, and to burn incense to him|Nolite (inquiens) negligere, filii mei; vos elegit Dominus ut stetis coram eo, et ministretis ei, colatisque eum et cremetis ei incensum]]. This incense, then, which the younger priests could offer, Zachary placed, kindling the *thymiama* with the said coals and placing that incense upon the altar of incense, which is also called the golden altar[[Ex 40:5||]].

paras.t: Et omnis multitudo populi erat orans foris, id est extra templum, puta in atrio, quia non licuit secundum legem populo ingredi Sancta, aut Sancta sanctorum, hoc est primam aut secundam partem templi. Porro, in templo fuit quotidie duplex sacrificium, unum de mane, aliud in vespere: et juxta hoc fuit quotidie duplex hora incensi, videlicet mane, et vespere. Nihilominus per antonomasiam hora incensi dicebatur dies Expiationis, quia tunc solennius offerebatur omni populo confluente, foris tamen manente, ad insinuandum quod sacerdos profundius debet penetrare divina quam populus: quod potissimum pertinet ad prælatum atque pastorem, cujus comparatione populus grex vocatur. Et de hac hora incensi quidam exponunt quod subditur: Hora incensi. Glossa etenim ait: Ista solennitas septimo mense celebrabatur, hoc est decima die Septembris, et dies Expiationis seu propitiationis nominabatur, quando solus pontifex intrabat secundum tabernaculum, scilicet Sancta sanctorum, cum sanguine. Sed hæc Glossa procedit secundum expositionem Ambrosii et Bedæ, opinantium Zachariam fuisse pontificem. Unde et Beda ait: Incensum in Sancta sanctorum a pontifice deferri, exspectante extra templum omni populo, decimo die septimi mensis, et hanc diem Expiationis seu propitiationis vocari Dominus jussit: cujus diei mysterium Apostolus ad Hebræos pandens, Jesum ostendit pontificem verum, utpote per pontificem legalem significatum: qui Jesus in sanguine proprio cœli secreta introiit, ut propitium nobis faceret Patrem, et interpellaret pro peccatis eorum qui adhuc præ foribus orantes exspectant.
paras.en: [[1:10|And all the multitude of the people was praying without|Et omnis multitudo populi erat orans foris]], that is, outside the temple, namely in the court; because by the law the people were not permitted to enter the Holy place or the Holy of holies, that is, the first or the second part of the temple. Now in the temple there was every day a twofold sacrifice, one in the morning and the other in the evening; and accordingly there was every day a twofold hour of incense, namely morning and evening[[Ex 30:7||]]. Nevertheless, by antonomasia [the use of a general name for one thing in particular, as the chief of its kind] the day of Expiation was called the hour of incense, because it was then offered more solemnly, with all the people flocking together, yet remaining outside[[Lev 16:17||]], to signify that the priest ought to penetrate divine things more deeply than the people: which belongs above all to the prelate and pastor, in comparison with whom the people are called a flock[[Jer 10:21||]][[Ezech 34:2||]][[Mich 7:14||]]. And some explain what follows, [[1:10|the hour of incense|Hora incensi]], of this hour of incense. For the Gloss says: This solemnity was celebrated in the seventh month, that is, on the tenth day of September[[Lev 16:29||]], and was called the day of Expiation or propitiation, when the high priest alone entered into the second tabernacle, that is, the Holy of holies, with blood[[Lev 16:14||]]. But this Gloss follows the exposition of Ambrose and Bede, who hold that Zachary was the high priest. Hence Bede too says: The Lord commanded that incense should be carried by the high priest into the Holy of holies, all the people waiting outside the temple, on the tenth day of the seventh month, and that this day should be called the day of Expiation or propitiation; and the Apostle, unfolding the mystery of this day to the Hebrews[[Heb 9:12||]], shows Jesus to be the true high priest, signified by the high priest of the law: Jesus, who in His own blood entered into the secret places of heaven, to make the Father propitious to us, and to intercede for the sins of those who still wait praying before the doors.

paras.t: Itaque advertendum, quod præter incensum præfatum quod ab inferioribus sacerdotibus ponebatur, fuit adhuc aliud incensum, quod soli pontifici licuit exercere seu ponere intra Sancta sanctorum in die Expiationis. Verum hoc non ponebatur ad offerendum, sed ut nebula inde ascendens operiret oraculum, dum contra illud adspergebat sacerdos sanguine vituli, et hirci pro populi peccatis oblati. De quo incenso non est hic sermo, secundum eos qui dicunt Zachariam non fuisse pontificem: quod quamvis concederetur, non tamen proprie affirmare censentur, quod fuit sacerdos simplex, et de minoribus unus, quia ut patet ex dictis, ad minus fuit unus de viginti quatuor principalioribus sacerdotibus, itemque in sua familia quæ de Abia descendit, superior, quamvis comparatione pontificis, simplex et minor possit dici sacerdos.
paras.en: It is to be noted, then, that besides the said incense, which was placed by the lower priests, there was yet another incense, which the high priest alone was allowed to offer, or place, within the Holy of holies on the day of Expiation. This, however, was not placed there as an offering, but so that the cloud rising from it might cover the oracle[[Lev 16:13||]], while the priest sprinkled towards it the blood of the calf[[Lev 16:14||]], and of the goat offered for the sins of the people[[Lev 16:15||]]. Of this incense there is no question here, according to those who say that Zachary was not the high priest. But even if this be granted, they are not to be taken as properly affirming that he was a simple priest and one of the lesser ones; for, as is clear from what has been said, he was at least one of the twenty-four chief priests, and also the head of his own family, which descended from Abia, although in comparison with the high priest he may be called a simple and lesser priest.

paras.t: Apparuit autem illi angelus Domini, scilicet Gabriel, ut infra patebit. Denique secundum Ambrosium, in Scripturis Deus et angeli apparere dicuntur, quoniam improvise et repentine videntur, ita quod eorum adspectus prævideri non valet seu præsentiri sive præsciri. Stans in corpore quod assumpsit, a dextris altaris incensi, de quo altari atque incenso jam habitum est. Stetit equidem juxta dextram partem altaris super quod Zacharias incensum ponebat. Et apte ad dextram stetit, quoniam dignior situs angelo lucis congruebat, et per dextram prosperitas, pietas et consolatio designantur. Angelus autem saluberrima et gaudiosissima annuntiare advenit, quia non solum Joannis, sed et Christi denuntiavit ortum sive adventum, summam quoque divinæ pietatis gratiam instare disseruit. Rursus, quoniam sacerdoti apparuit, et Christi, qui est summus sacerdos verumque sacrificium, nuntiavit adventum, rite in templo angelus apparebat; item, ad ostendendum quam gratum sit Deo sacerdotem in templi obsequio devote ac sedule occupari, quanta etiam sit dignitas ordinis et officii sacerdotalis.
paras.en: [[1:11|And there appeared to him an angel of the Lord|Apparuit autem illi angelus Domini]], namely Gabriel, as will appear below. Further, according to Ambrose, God and the angels are said in the Scriptures to *appear*, because they are seen unexpectedly and suddenly, so that their appearing cannot be foreseen, nor sensed or known beforehand. [[1:11|standing|Stans]] in the body that he had assumed, [[1:11|on the right side of the altar of incense|a dextris altaris incensi]], of which altar and incense we have already spoken. He stood, that is, beside the right-hand side of the altar on which Zachary was laying the incense. And fittingly he stood on the right, since the worthier place became an angel of light, and by the right hand prosperity, loving-kindness and consolation are signified. For the angel came to announce things most wholesome and most joyful, since he foretold the birth or coming not of John only, but also of Christ, and declared that the supreme grace of the divine loving-kindness was at hand. Again, since he appeared to a priest, and announced the coming of Christ, who is the high priest and the true sacrifice[[Heb 4:14||]][[Heb 7:26||]][[Heb 9:11||]], the angel fittingly appeared in the temple; and also to show how pleasing it is to God that a priest be devoutly and diligently occupied in the service of the temple, and how great is the dignity of the priestly order and office.

paras.t: Et Zacharias turbatus est, videns angelum tam splendentem, et timor irruit super eum, hoc est, incidit, et ex superiori causa incidit cordi ejus ex insolita visione. Connaturale est namque fragilitati humanæ ex visione cœlestium civium aut spirituum defunctorum vehementer mirari, immutari, turbari, vereri, quia ignotum, rarum, insolitumque consistit quod accidit, et quia alterius conditionis seu altioris potestatis est quod apparet: ita quod homo frequenter primo occursu ignorat quid sit, aut cur venerit, propter quod sæpe de proprio pavet periculo, atque de rei exitu contremiscit. Angeli quoque cum inconsueto splendore atque fulgureo vultu apparere solent. Unde et Daniel ait ad angelum: Domine, in visione tua dissolutæ sunt compages meæ; sed et halitus meus intercluditur, et nihil in me remansit virium. Hinc Prophetæ mirabilibus Dei conspectis cadere consueverunt, juxta illud Ezechielis: Vidi, et cecidi super faciem meam. Ambrosius quoque hic ait: Utinam et nobis ad altaria sacrificium deferentibus adsistat angelus, imo præbeat se videndum. Non enim dubites adsistere angelum, quando Christus immolatur. Iterum ait: Perturbamur et a nostro alienamur affectu, quando perstringimur alicujus superioris potestatis occursu. Idem fatetur Chrysostomus, dicens: Non potest homo quantumcumque sit justus, absque timore cernere angelum. Hinc Zacharias adspectum non tolerans præsentis angeli, nec fulgorem illum valens sufferre, turbatur.
paras.en: [[1:12|And Zachary seeing him, was troubled|Et Zacharias turbatus est]], seeing the angel so resplendent, [[1:12|and fear fell upon him|et timor irruit super eum]], that is, came upon him, and came upon his heart from a higher cause, through the unwonted vision. For it is natural to human frailty to marvel exceedingly, to be changed, troubled and afraid at the sight of the citizens of heaven or of the spirits of the dead, because what happens is unknown, rare and unwonted, and because what appears is of another condition or of a higher power: so that a man often does not know at the first encounter what it is or why it has come, and therefore often fears for his own danger and trembles at how the matter will end. Angels, too, are wont to appear with an unaccustomed splendour and a face like lightning. Whence Daniel also says to the angel: Lord, [[Dan 10:16|at the sight of thee my joints are loosed|in visione tua dissolutæ sunt compages meæ]]; [[Dan 10:17|moreover, my breath is stopped|sed et halitus meus intercluditur]], [[Dan 10:16|and no strength hath remained in me|et nihil in me remansit virium]]. Hence the Prophets, when they beheld the wonders of God, were wont to fall down, according to that of Ezechiel: [[Ezech 2:1|and I saw, and I fell upon my face|Vidi, et cecidi super faciem meam]] [the margin's chapter number is unclear; the same words occur also at Ezech 3:23 and 43:3]. Ambrose too says here: Would that an angel might stand by us also as we bring the sacrifice to the altars, nay, might show himself to be seen! For do not doubt that an angel stands by when Christ is immolated. Again he says: We are troubled and taken out of our own state of mind when we are struck by the encounter of some higher power. Chrysostom says the same: A man, however just he may be, cannot behold an angel without fear. Hence Zachary, not bearing the sight of the angel present, nor able to endure that brightness, is troubled.

paras.t: Quibus consonat Origenes: Nova (inquiens) facies humanis se obtutibus præbens turbat mentem, animumque consternat. Hinc angelus sciens hanc humanam esse naturam, primum perturbationi medetur. Nam subditur: Ait autem ad illum angelus: Ne timeas, Zacharia. Ait quippe Athanasius in vita S. Antonii: Non difficilis est bonorum spirituum malorumque discretio. Si enim post timorem successerit gaudium, a Domino venisse sciamus auxilium, quia securitas animæ signum est majestatis præsentis; si autem incussa formido permanserit, hostis est qui videtur. Hinc asserit Beda: Sicut humanæ (inquiens) defectionis est terreri, sic angelicæ dignitatis est de suo adspectu paventem blandiendo consolari. Econtra dæmones, quos de sua præsentia territos sentiunt, ampliore terrore commovent.
paras.en: With this Origen agrees: A new face presenting itself to human sight troubles the mind and dismays the soul. Hence the angel, knowing that this is human nature, first heals the disturbance. For there follows: [[1:13|But the angel said to him: Fear not, Zachary|Ait autem ad illum angelus: Ne timeas, Zacharia]]. For Athanasius says in the life of St Antony: The discerning of good and evil spirits is not difficult. For if joy follows after fear, let us know that help has come from the Lord, since the soul's calm is a sign of the majesty present; but if the fear struck into us remains, it is the enemy that is seen. Hence Bede declares: As it belongs to human weakness to be terrified, so it belongs to the angelic dignity to console with gentleness one who is afraid at the sight of him. The demons, on the contrary, stir up with greater terror those whom they perceive to be terrified by their presence.

paras.t: Itaque, Ne timeas, id est, timor immoderatus qui actum impedit rationis, omnisque turbatio mentis tollens quietem, recedat a te, estoque consolatus et gaudens in Domino. Id itaque angelicæ bonitatis, caritatis, pietatisque est, ut hominem bonum, non induratum ac reprobum, sua visione inquietatum, tremefactum, turbatum, victum, dejectum, tranquillet, consoletur, confortet: quemadmodum diabolicæ impietatis est, incussum augere timorem, ut rectæ rationis impediatur judicium. Verumtamen, sæpenumero Satanas in angelum lucis transfiguratus, hominibus apparuisse legitur, et nihilo minus verba blanda ac consolatoria protulisse, ut per hoc desuper venisse crederetur, sicut in vita S. Martini narratur; sed mentem interius directe consolari et confortare non valet, quia nec immediate atque directe agit in eam, quemadmodum angelus eam illuminando.
paras.en: So: [[1:13|Fear not|Ne timeas]], that is, let immoderate fear, which hinders the act of reason, and every disturbance of mind that takes away its quiet, depart from thee, and be thou consoled and rejoicing in the Lord[[Is 61:10||]]. It belongs, then, to the goodness, charity and loving-kindness of the angels to calm, console and strengthen a good man (not a hardened and reprobate one) who has been disquieted, made to tremble, troubled, overcome and cast down by the sight of them; just as it belongs to the wickedness of the devil to increase the fear he has struck into a man, so that the judgment of right reason may be hindered. Yet we read that Satan, transformed into an angel of light[[2 Cor 11:14||]], has very often appeared to men and has nonetheless spoken soothing and consoling words, so that he might thereby be believed to have come from above, as is told in the life of St Martin; but he cannot directly console and strengthen the mind within, because he does not act upon it immediately and directly, as an angel does in enlightening it.

paras.t: Exaudita est deprecatio tua, quam nunc in sacrificando et incensum ponendo corde et ore fudisti. Dicunt aliqui, quod non solum pro Christi adventu, sed et pro filio exoravit. Augustinus vero in libro de Quæstionibus Evangelii, contradicit et dicit: Nemo orat accipere, quod se accepturum desperat. Usquequo autem desperavit se filium habiturum, quod nec angelo filium promittenti crediderit. Probabile tamen est, quod jam ante frequenter pro hac re deprecatus sit Dominum: sicut et Isaac oravit pro sobole, cernens quod conjux sua sterilis esset, ut patet in Genesi; Anna quoque, ut in libro Regum legitur, et alii Sancti veteris Testamenti. Tunc enim grande coram hominibus fuit opprobrium, conjugii fructu carere. Insuper Zacharias, ut aliqui dicunt, oravit etiam pro liberatione Judæorum a dominatu Herodis et alienigenarum, tributoque Romanorum. Certius autem tenendum est, quod pro adventu Messiæ totis oravit præcordiis, et pro spirituali salute.
paras.en: [[1:13|thy prayer is heard|Exaudita est deprecatio tua]], the prayer which thou hast now poured out with heart and lips in sacrificing and laying the incense. Some say that he prayed not only for the coming of Christ but also for a son. But Augustine, in the book of Questions on the Gospel, contradicts this and says: No one prays to receive what he despairs of receiving. And he had despaired of having a son so far that he did not believe even the angel when he promised one. Yet it is probable that he had often prayed the Lord for this before: as Isaac too prayed for offspring, seeing that his wife was barren, as is clear in Genesis[[Gen 25:21||]]; and Anna, as we read in the book of Kings[[1 Kings 1:10||]], and other Saints of the Old Testament. For at that time it was a great reproach before men to be without the fruit of marriage. Moreover Zachary, as some say, prayed also for the deliverance of the Jews from the rule of Herod and of foreigners, and from the tribute of the Romans. But it is to be held more surely that he prayed with his whole heart for the coming of the Messias, and for spiritual salvation.

paras.t: Et quoniam Deus liberalissimus dator ac exauditor est et munificentissimus benefactor, abundantia pietatis suæ merita supplicum excedens et vota seu desideria, non solum demonstrat se Zachariam audisse, imo et plura quam petiit se daturum testatur, utpote filium tam electum, tantaque gratiarum charismata universæ Israeliticæ plebi per eum. Nam subditur: Et Elisabeth uxor tua pariet tibi filium. Convenienter angelus nomen conjugis Zachariæ expressit, ne de alia se putaret filium habiturum, eo quod ista vetula esset ac sterilis. Et vocabis, id est, esse dices, seu vocando exprimes, nomen ejus Joannes. Vel, Vocabis nomen ejus nominatum, id est rem ipsam seu filium tuum, Joannem, id est nomine hoc nominante, quod est Joannes. Itaque propter certitudinem prophetiæ nomen filii nascituri exprimitur, et propter sanctitatem ac dignitatem ejus futuram, item ob nominis interpretationem rei significatæ convenientem. Joannes namque, in quo est gratia, interpretatur. Recte ergo Joannes vocari præcipitur, cui tanta fuerat gratia danda, ut de ipso Christus testatus sit: Inter natos mulierum non surrexit major Joanne Baptista. Qui et Christum, per quem gratia et veritas facta est, cecinit adfuturum, et monstravit præsentem. Denique, sex hominum nomina prænuntiata leguntur in veteri Testamento, videlicet: Isaac, Samsonis (in libro Judicum, secundum aliam translationem, ut aliqui dicunt: translatio namque Hieronymi ita non habet), Josiæ, ut in libris Regum patet. Hi tres sancti fuerunt. Item Ismaelis, Agag, et Cyri, quos reprobos fuisse asseritur: quod de duobus ultimis constat.
paras.en: And since God is a most liberal giver and hearer of prayer and a most munificent benefactor, exceeding by the abundance of his loving-kindness the merits of those who pray, and their vows or desires, he not only shows that he has heard Zachary, but even declares that he will give more than he asked, namely a son so chosen, and through him such great gifts of grace to the whole people of Israel. For there follows: [[1:13|and thy wife Elizabeth shall bear thee a son|Et Elisabeth uxor tua pariet tibi filium]]. The angel fittingly named Zachary's wife, lest he should think he would have a son by another, since she was old and barren. [[1:13|And thou shalt call|Et vocabis]], that is, thou shalt say it to be, or express by calling, [[1:13|his name John|nomen ejus Joannes]]. Or: thou shalt call *his name*, meaning the one named, that is, the thing itself, thy son, *John*, that is, by the naming of this name, which is John [Denis explains the Latin *vocabis nomen ejus Joannes* in two ways: either "thou shalt declare that his name is John", or "thou shalt call the one so named, thy son, John"; a footnote in the edition gives the variant *Joannem*]. So the name of the son to be born is expressed because of the certainty of the prophecy, and because of his future holiness and dignity, and also because the meaning of the name fits the thing signified. For *John* is interpreted *in whom is grace*. Rightly, then, he is commanded to be called John, to whom so great a grace was to be given that Christ testified of him: [[Matt 11:11|there hath not risen among them that are born of women a greater than John the Baptist|Inter natos mulierum non surrexit major Joanne Baptista]]. He it was who sang that Christ, through whom [[John 1:17|grace and truth came|gratia et veritas facta est]], was about to come, and pointed Him out when He was present. Lastly, we read in the Old Testament that the names of six men were foretold, namely: Isaac[[Gen 17:19||]]; Samson (in the book of Judges[[Judg 13:1||]], according to another translation, as some say, for Jerome's translation does not have it so); Josias, as is clear in the books of Kings[[3 Kings 13:2||]]. These three were holy. Likewise of Ismael[[Gen 16:11||]], Agag[[Num 24:7||]] and Cyrus[[Is 45:1||]], who are said to have been reprobate: which is certain of the last two.

paras.t: Et erit tibi gaudium et exsultatio, id est, in nativitate ejus tanta tibi in mente lætitia erit, quod redundabit in corpus, vultuque hilaris apparebis, et ex magnitudine gloriationis tuæ tota tua natura suaviter reflorebit: non ob id dumtaxat, quod filius tibi sit natus, sed quoniam filius talis ac tantus, tamque prælectus a Deo; sicque implebitur in te illud Sapientis: Exsultat gaudio pater justi; et qui genuit sapientem, lætabitur in eo. Rursusque scriptum est: Gloria patris, filius sapiens. Præterea, quantum de bono gloriandum sit filio, patet per illud Ecclesiastici: Ne jucunderis in filiis impiis, si multiplicantur; melior est unus timens Deum, quam mille filii impii; et utile est mori sine filiis, quam relinquere filios impios. Dicit quoque Ambrosius: Admonentur hoc loco parentes gratias agere Deo, tam pro ortu quam pro meritis filiorum: non enim mediocre Dei munus est dare liberos propagatores generis, successionis heredes. Divinum igitur munus fecunditas est parentis.
paras.en: [[1:14|And thou shalt have joy and gladness|Et erit tibi gaudium et exsultatio]], that is, at his birth there will be such gladness in thy mind that it will overflow into the body, and thou wilt appear cheerful of countenance, and from the greatness of thy rejoicing thy whole nature will sweetly flower again: not only because a son has been born to thee, but because he is a son of such quality and so great, and so specially chosen by God; and thus will be fulfilled in thee that saying of the Wise man: [[Prov 23:24|The father of the just rejoiceth greatly: he that hath begotten a wise son, shall have joy in him.|Exsultat gaudio pater justi; et qui genuit sapientem, lætabitur in eo]]. And again it is written: A wise son is the glory of his father[[Prov 10:1||]]. Moreover, how much one should glory in a good son is clear from that of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 16:1|Rejoice not in ungodly children, if they be multiplied|Ne jucunderis in filiis impiis, si multiplicantur]]; [[Ecclus 16:3|better is one that feareth God, than a thousand ungodly children|melior est unus timens Deum, quam mille filii impii]]; [[Ecclus 16:4|And it is better to die without children, than to leave ungodly children.|et utile est mori sine filiis, quam relinquere filios impios]]. Ambrose too says: Parents are here admonished to give thanks to God both for the birth and for the merits of their children: for it is no mean gift of God to give children who carry on the race, heirs to succeed them. Fruitfulness, then, is a divine gift to a parent.

paras.t: Et multi in nativitate ejus gaudebunt, videlicet cognati tui, amici atque vicini. Quos multæ causæ ad congratulationem hanc induxerunt: Primo, quoniam Zacharias et Elisabeth omnibus singulariter cari fuerunt, idcirco eorum prosperitati et gaudio congaudebant. Secundo, propter novitatem magnitudinemque miraculi, quod videbant in puero supernaturaliter edito. Tertio, quia in puero nato consideraverunt divinam fuisse visionem impletam, quam habuit Zacharias. Quarto, quia sperabant hunc puerum magnæ fore utilitatis et gratiæ, ita quod totus populus Judæorum ex ipso proficeret atque divinitus juvaretur per ipsum. Denique singulis annis in natalitio ejus omnes Christiani specialiter gloriantur, quod tanti Sancti societatem sortiti sunt, et quia in peccato natus non fuit ut ceteri Sancti communiter, sed mundatus et sanctificatus fuit in utero matris. A Sarracenis quoque ejus nativitas festivatur. Hinc ratio gaudii subditur:
paras.en: [[1:14|and many shall rejoice in his nativity|Et multi in nativitate ejus gaudebunt]], namely thy kinsfolk, friends and neighbours. Many causes led them to this rejoicing together: first, because Zachary and Elizabeth were singularly dear to all, and so they rejoiced with them in their good fortune and joy; secondly, because of the novelty and greatness of the miracle which they saw in the child born beyond the course of nature; thirdly, because in the birth of the child they perceived that the divine vision which Zachary had had was fulfilled; fourthly, because they hoped that this child would be of great profit and grace, so that the whole people of the Jews would advance through him and be divinely helped by him. Lastly, every year on his birthday all Christians glory in a special way that they have been granted the fellowship of so great a Saint, and because he was not born in sin, as the other Saints commonly are, but was cleansed and sanctified in his mother's womb. His nativity is kept as a feast by the Saracens too. Then the reason for the joy is added:

paras.t: Erit enim magnus, magnitudine spirituali, quæ est magnitudo gratiæ et sapientiæ ac virtutis, ita quod esse majorem, est esse perfectiorem; coram Domino, id est vere, ita quod Deus judicabit eum talem. Quidam vero magni sunt, non utique coram Deo, sed coram propriis oculis et coram hominibus, sicut hypocritæ et superbi, quorum cuilibet dicitur: Depone magnitudinem tuam absque tribulatione. Quis autem beatissimi hujus Joannis magnitudinem possit exprimere? Sed angelus consequenter eam declarat; et Christus unico testimonio complexus est multa: Inter natos (inquiens) mulierum non surrexit major Joanne Baptista. Insuper, secundum Ambrosium, sicut corporis, ita et animæ numeramus ætates, non ratione temporis, sed qualitate et gradu virtutis: ut vir perfectus ille dicatur, qui pueritiæ caret errore, et lubricum adolescentiæ animi maturitate transcendit; pusillus autem, qui nullum adhuc virtutis habet processum. Postremo, secundum quatuor dimensiones corporales, spiritualis quoque magnitudo in quatuor proportionaliter consistit, puta in altitudine conversationis seu contemplationis, vel dilectionis divinæ, in latitudine caritatis fraternæ, in profunditate humiliationis, in longitudine perseverantiæ usque in finem: secundum illud Apostoli ad Ephesios, Ut possitis comprehendere cum omnibus Sanctis, quæ sit longitudo, et latitudo, et sublimitas, et profundum.
paras.en: [[1:15|For he shall be great|Erit enim magnus]] with spiritual greatness, which is the greatness of grace, wisdom and virtue, so that to be greater is to be more perfect; [[1:15|before the Lord|coram Domino]], that is, truly, so that God will judge him to be such. Some, indeed, are great, not before God but in their own eyes and before men, like hypocrites and the proud, to each of whom it is said: [[Job 36:19|Lay down thy greatness without tribulation|Depone magnitudinem tuam absque tribulatione]]. But who could express the greatness of this most blessed John? The angel, however, goes on to declare it; and Christ embraced much in a single testimony, saying: [[Matt 11:11|there hath not risen among them that are born of women a greater than John the Baptist|Inter natos (inquiens) mulierum non surrexit major Joanne Baptista]]. Moreover, according to Ambrose, as we number the ages of the body, so also those of the soul, not by reckoning of time but by the quality and degree of virtue: so that he is called a perfect man who is free from the error of childhood and rises above the slipperiness of youth by maturity of mind; but he a little one who has as yet made no progress in virtue. Lastly, after the four bodily dimensions, spiritual greatness too consists proportionately in four: namely in the height of one's way of life or of contemplation, or of the love of God; in the breadth of brotherly charity; in the depth of humility; in the length of perseverance unto the end: according to that of the Apostle to the Ephesians, that [[Eph 3:18|You may be able to comprehend, with all the saints, what is the breadth and length and height and depth,|Ut possitis comprehendere cum omnibus Sanctis, quæ sit longitudo, et latitudo, et sublimitas, et profundum]].

paras.t: Vinum et siceram non bibet. Secundum Bedam, per siceram Judæi intelligunt omnem potum inebriativum, de quacumque sit confectus materia: per quod austeritas vitæ Joannis parcitasque signantur. In libro Judicum quoque hæc pocula leguntur Samsoni prohibita, quoniam nazaræus Dei fuit ab utero matris usque ad diem mortis. Joannes vero sublimius fuit nazaræus Dei, id est Deo consecratus toto tempore vitæ suæ, ideo per omne tempus suæ vitæ ab his abstinuit potibus: sicut in lege abstinebant ab his Nazaræi tempore consecrationis separationisve suæ, et postea vinum bibere potuerunt, ut in libro Numerorum describitur. Decuit autem Joannem tantæ abstinentiæ esse, ut testimonium ejus de Christo credibilius redderetur, insinuaretque per vitæ suæ rigorem, quod Christus in primo suo adventu temporalium abundantiam et corporum oblectamenta non esset daturus, ut obtenebratissimi præstolantur Judæi.
paras.en: [[1:15|shall drink no wine nor strong drink|Vinum et siceram non bibet]]. According to Bede, the Jews understand by *sicera* [strong drink] every intoxicating drink, of whatever matter it be made: by which the austerity and sparingness of John's life are signified. In the book of Judges too we read that these drinks were forbidden to Samson[[Judg 13:4||]], since he was a Nazarite of God from his mother's womb until the day of his death[[Judg 13:7||]]. But John was a Nazarite of God in a higher way, that is, consecrated to God for the whole time of his life; and therefore he abstained from these drinks for the whole time of his life: as under the Law the Nazarites abstained from them for the time of their consecration or separation[[Num 6:3||]], and afterwards could drink wine, as is described in the book of Numbers[[Num 6:20||]]. And it was fitting that John should be of so great abstinence, so that his testimony of Christ might be made more credible, and that he might intimate by the rigour of his life that Christ in his first coming would not give an abundance of temporal goods and the delights of the body, as the utterly benighted Jews await.

paras.t: Et Spiritu Sancto replebitur, hoc est gratia, donisque Spiritus Sancti, adhuc ex utero matris suæ, id est in utero maternali, seu antequam egrediatur ex eo: qua gratia a peccato originali purgabitur, et donis Spiritus Sancti anima ejus ornabitur, atque ad operandum meritorie disponetur, quemadmodum Dominus loquitur de Jeremia: Antequam exires de ventre sanctificavi te. Et per utriusque in utero sanctificationem omnimoda sanctificatio, innocentia ac puritas Christi in utero virginali est præfigurata. Verumtamen major et gratiosior fuit sanctificatio Joannis quam Jeremiæ, sicut et ejus nativitas ac persona propinquiores fuerant Christo: quod et ex ipso modo loquendi sacræ Scripturæ elicitur. Non enim de Jeremia assertum est, quod Spiritu Sancto repleretur in utero. Præterea, quum Spiritus Sanctus sit verus incircumscriptusque Deus, certum est quod per essentiam sit ubique. Nihilo minus in peccatoribus esse negatur, quia per gratiam eis non inest. Propter quod in Proverbiis legitur: Longe est Dominus ab impiis; itemque: Spiritus sanctus disciplinæ effugiet fictum, et auferet se a cogitationibus quæ sunt sine intellectu. Hinc Spiritus Sanctus illis dicitur infundi et dari, quibus dona ejus ad gratiam gratum facientem spectantia infunduntur ac dantur, quos et inhabitat quamdiu in caritate et gratia manent; illos vero fertur implere, quos singulari et abundanti perficit gratia. Ideo dicit Ambrosius: Cui Spiritus Sanctus infunditur, magnarum est plenitudo virtutum.
paras.en: [[1:15|and he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost|Et Spiritu Sancto replebitur]], that is, with the grace and gifts of the Holy Ghost, [[1:15|even from his mother's womb|adhuc ex utero matris suæ]], that is, in his mother's womb, or before he comes forth from it: by which grace he will be cleansed from original sin, and his soul will be adorned with the gifts of the Holy Ghost and disposed to act meritoriously, as the Lord says of Jeremias: [[Jer 1:5|before thou camest forth out of the womb, I sanctified thee|Antequam exires de ventre sanctificavi te]]. And by the sanctification of each of them in the womb, the entire sanctification, innocence and purity of Christ in the virginal womb was prefigured. Yet the sanctification of John was greater and more full of grace than that of Jeremias, as his birth and person also were nearer to Christ: which is drawn also from the very manner of speaking of Holy Scripture. For it is not said of Jeremias that he was filled with the Holy Ghost in the womb. Further, since the Holy Ghost is true and uncircumscribed God, it is certain that he is everywhere by his essence. Nevertheless he is said not to be in sinners, because he is not in them by grace. For this reason we read in Proverbs: [[Prov 15:29|The Lord is far from the wicked|Longe est Dominus ab impiis]]; and again: [[Wis 1:5|the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee from the deceitful, and will withdraw himself from thoughts that are without understanding|Spiritus sanctus disciplinæ effugiet fictum, et auferet se a cogitationibus quæ sunt sine intellectu]]. Hence the Holy Ghost is said to be poured into and given to those into whom his gifts that belong to sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes a man pleasing to God] are poured and given, and whom he also indwells as long as they abide in charity and grace; but he is said to *fill* those whom he perfects with singular and abundant grace. Therefore Ambrose says: He into whom the Holy Ghost is poured has the fulness of great virtues.

paras.t: Deinde efficacia doctrinæ Joannis ostenditur. Et multos filiorum Israel convertet ad Dominum Deum ipsorum, id est ad Christum, de quo protinus subditur: Et ipse præcedet ante illum, hoc est ante Christum: cujus fuit præcursor, ejus adventum annuntiando, ipsumque monstrando, ac aliis modis populum ad Christi fidem disponendo, utpote baptizando, impios increpando, et omnes ad se confluentes ad virtutes hortando, prout infra in textu narrabitur. Per hoc autem quod angelus Christum nominat Dominum Deum Israel, confunditur hæresis Arii, negans quod Christus sit verus Deus; insania quoque Manichæi dicentis, alium esse Deum legis seu Judæorum, et alium Evangelii seu Christianorum; perfidiaque Photini, Christum ex Maria incepisse, nec ante fuisse, dicentis. Itaque, ante Christum præcessit et suo baptismo Christi Baptismum, sua passione Christi occisionem, suo ad limbum descensu Christi descensum ad eumdem, præcucurrit et præsignavit. In spiritu et virtute Eliæ, id est tali gratia et fortitudine a Spiritu Sancto concessis, in quali Spiritus Sancti gratia et virtute Elias fecit opera virtuosa quæ de ipso in libris Regum scribuntur, atque secundum Christi præcedet adventum, ut Malachias habet; vel, In spiritu prophetiæ et gratia, et virtute justitiæ, quibus fulsit et vixit Elias. Uterque equidem Propheta et eremita ac fervens zelator justitiæ fuit. Et sicut Elias redarguit Achab regem et Jezabel conjugem ejus, sic Joannes Herodem et Herodiadem. In asperitate quoque vestitus et victus convenientiam præcipuam habuerunt. Secundum Augustinum autem, non ait, In anima Eliæ, quoniam animæ non transcorporantur, sed, In spiritu et virtute Eliæ: Spiritus enim qui fuit in Elia, venit in Joannem, et similiter virtus ejus.
paras.en: Next the efficacy of John's teaching is shown. [[1:16|he shall convert many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God|Et multos filiorum Israel convertet ad Dominum Deum ipsorum]], that is, to Christ, of whom it is added straightway: [[1:17|And he shall go before him|Et ipse præcedet ante illum]], that is, before Christ, whose forerunner he was: by announcing His coming, by pointing Him out, and by disposing the people to the faith of Christ in other ways, namely by baptizing, by rebuking the wicked, and by exhorting all who flocked to him to the virtues, as will be told below in the text[[Luke 3:3||]]. And by the angel's calling Christ the Lord God of Israel, the heresy of Arius is confounded, which denies that Christ is true God; so too the madness of Manichæus, who said that the God of the Law, or of the Jews, is one, and the God of the Gospel, or of the Christians, another; and the perfidy of Photinus, who said that Christ began from Mary and did not exist before. So he went before Christ: by his baptism he ran ahead of and foreshadowed the Baptism of Christ, by his passion the slaying of Christ, by his descent into limbo Christ's descent to the same place. [[1:17|in the spirit and power of Elias|In spiritu et virtute Eliæ]], that is, with such grace and strength, granted by the Holy Ghost, as the grace and power of the Holy Ghost in which Elias did the mighty works written of him in the books of Kings; and Elias will go before the second coming of Christ, as Malachias has it[[Mal 4:5||]]. Or, in the spirit of prophecy and grace, and in the power of justice, in which Elias shone and lived. For each was a prophet and a hermit and a fervent zealot for justice. And as Elias rebuked king Achab and Jezabel his wife[[3 Kings 18:18||]][[3 Kings 21:20||]], so John rebuked Herod and Herodias. In the roughness of their clothing and food, too, they were especially alike. But, according to Augustine, he does not say, In the soul of Elias, since souls do not pass from one body into another, but, In the spirit and power of Elias: for the Spirit that was in Elias came into John, and likewise his power.

paras.t: Ut convertat corda patrum in filios, id est, Judæos sui temporis faciat Patriarchis et Prophetis olim defunctis amabiles et conformes, inducendo eos ad fidem et gratiam ac Christi Baptismum: per quæ patres illi reputabunt istos vere amandos, et corda sua convertent per amorem ad istos. Vel, per corda patrum intelliguntur veræ ac spirituales intelligentiæ Scripturarum: quas intelligentias præfati patres sortiti sunt. Tunc ergo Joannes corda patrum illorum convertit ad filios, id est ad Judæos quibus personaliter prædicavit, quando illorum spiritualem scientiam istis communicavit seu prædicavit. Rursus, patres intelligi possunt progenitores seu majores discipulorum Apostolorumque Christi: qui primo contra Evangelium sæviebant, postea vero per Joannem et Apostolos sunt conversi, et filiis suis præfatis concordes effecti. Denique, istud Elias est facturus circa secundum Christi adventum, sicut per Malachiam Dominus contestatur: Ecce ego (inquiens) mittam vobis Eliam prophetam, antequam veniat dies Domini magnus et horribilis: et convertet cor patrum ad filios, et cor filiorum ad patres eorum. Et incredulos, id est perfidos Judæos, convertet ad prudentiam justorum, hoc est veram sapientiam, evangelicamque doctrinam, et spiritualem intelligentiam Scripturarum, ne legem carnaliter intelligant, nec litteram, quæ occidit, sequantur. De qua prudentia ad Romanos asseritur: Prudentia spiritus vita et pax. Sed et vera discretio, prudentia est justorum, qua Deo rationabiliter obsequuntur, juxta illud Apostoli, Rationabile obsequium vestrum.
paras.en: [[1:17|that he may turn the hearts of the fathers unto the children|Ut convertat corda patrum in filios]], that is, that he may make the Jews of his own time dear to, and like, the Patriarchs and Prophets long dead, by leading them to faith and grace and to the Baptism of Christ: on account of which those fathers will hold them truly worthy of love, and will turn their hearts to them in love. Or, by the hearts of the fathers are understood the true and spiritual understandings of the Scriptures, which those fathers were given. John, then, turned the hearts of those fathers to the children, that is, to the Jews to whom he preached in person, when he imparted or preached to them their spiritual knowledge. Again, the fathers can be understood as the forebears or elders of the disciples and Apostles of Christ, who at first raged against the Gospel, but afterwards were converted by John and the Apostles, and made of one mind with those children of theirs. Lastly, Elias is to do this about the time of Christ's second coming, as the Lord testifies through Malachias, saying: [[Mal 4:5|Behold, I will send you Elias the prophet, before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord|Ecce ego (inquiens) mittam vobis Eliam prophetam, antequam veniat dies Domini magnus et horribilis]]: [[Mal 4:6|And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers|et convertet cor patrum ad filios, et cor filiorum ad patres eorum]]. [[1:17|and the incredulous|Et incredulos]], that is, the faithless Jews, he will convert [[1:17|to the wisdom of the just|ad prudentiam justorum]], that is, to true wisdom, the teaching of the Gospel, and the spiritual understanding of the Scriptures, that they may not understand the Law carnally, nor follow the letter, which killeth[[2 Cor 3:6||]]. Of this wisdom it is said to the Romans: [[Rom 8:6|the wisdom of the spirit is life and peace|Prudentia spiritus vita et pax]]. And true discretion, too, is the wisdom of the just, by which they serve God reasonably, according to that word of the Apostle: [[Rom 12:1|your reasonable service|Rationabile obsequium vestrum]].

paras.t: Quid autem sit ita convertere corda patrum in filios, atque incredulos ad justorum prudentiam, subditur: parare Domino plebem perfectam. Per hanc instructionem seu illuminationem et conversionem Judæorum, eos disponit ad evangelicæ legis observantiam stabilem et sinceram, per quod fiant plebs Christi perfecta. Quod maxime fuit impletum in Judæis post Christi ascensionem et Paracleti missionem per Apostolos in Jerusalem conversis, qui, sicut in Actibus Apostolorum habetur, Deo perfectissime servierunt: ad quam conversionem Joannes dispositive fuerat operatus. Nam multos illorum qui per Apostolos fuerunt plene conversi, ipse aliquo modo convertit, et ad fidem Christi disposuit, Christum venisse docendo, atque in nomine Christi venturi baptizando. Aliqui quoque ex Joannis discipulis Christo se conjunxerunt, sicut Andreas, et facti sunt plebs Christi perfecta. Hinc infra Zacharias loquitur ad Joannem: Præibis ante faciem Domini parare vias ejus, ad dandam scientiam salutis plebi ejus, in remissionem peccatorum eorum. Multi equidem per prædicationem Joannis crediderunt in Christum, quamvis postea circa Christi passionem atque in ea fuerint per sacerdotes, Scribas et Pharisæos seducti, et a Christo aversi: qui rursus misso Spiritu Sancto per Apostolos plenissime sunt conversi.
paras.en: What it is thus to turn the hearts of the fathers unto the children, and the incredulous to the wisdom of the just, is added: [[1:17|to prepare unto the Lord a perfect people|parare Domino plebem perfectam]]. By this instruction, or enlightening, and conversion of the Jews, he disposes them to a steadfast and sincere observance of the Gospel law, so that they may become Christ's perfect people. This was fulfilled above all in the Jews who were converted by the Apostles in Jerusalem after Christ's ascension and the sending of the Paraclete, and who, as we read in the Acts of the Apostles, served God most perfectly[[Acts 2:41||]][[Acts 4:32||]]: John had worked towards that conversion by preparing for it. For many of those who were fully converted by the Apostles he had in some measure converted himself, and disposed to the faith of Christ[[Luke 3:3||]], by teaching that Christ had come, and by baptizing in the name of the Christ who was to come. Some of John's disciples, too, joined themselves to Christ, as Andrew did[[John 1:40||]], and became Christ's perfect people. Hence below Zachary says to John: [[1:76|go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways|Præibis ante faciem Domini parare vias ejus]], [[1:77|To give knowledge of salvation to his people, unto the remission of their sins|ad dandam scientiam salutis plebi ejus, in remissionem peccatorum eorum]]. Many indeed believed in Christ through John's preaching, although afterwards, about the time of Christ's passion and during it, they were led astray by the priests, Scribes and Pharisees, and turned away from Christ; and these, when the Holy Ghost had been sent, were again most fully converted by the Apostles.

paras.t: Et dixit Zacharias ad angelum: Unde hoc sciam? id est, quo signo cognoscam certissime vera esse quæ promisisti? Mos etenim erat Judæis, audito aliquo admirando, quærere signum certificans, scilicet supernaturalem effectum, quo Deus testaretur seu declararet verum esse quod dicebatur, ut patet in Gedeone, Ezechia et aliis multis. Hæc autem locutus est Zacharias dubitando, quia non ad Dei omnipotentiam, sed ad naturæ cursum, naturalemque ordinem et causalitatem respexit, sicut sequentia pandunt eloquia. Ego enim sum senex, et uxor mea processit in diebus suis: quasi dicat, Præ senio steriles sumus. Non videtur Zacharias fuisse ambiguus de angeli qualitate, an scilicet fuerit spiritus bonus, an nequam: imo cognovit quod esset angelus lucis, quia in sacro loco ac cultu divino apparuit, tamque salubria nuntiavit, Dei honorem et communem salutem concernentia; et ex modo loquendi ac consolandi, quem habuit angelus, hoc ipsum pensavit. Quum ergo ista cognoverit, culpabile fuit quod discredens expetiit signum: ideo reprehenditur et punitur, tamen piissime.
paras.en: [[1:18|And Zachary said to the angel: Whereby shall I know this?|Et dixit Zacharias ad angelum: Unde hoc sciam?]] that is, by what sign shall I know most surely that what thou hast promised is true? For it was the custom of the Jews, on hearing something wonderful, to seek a sign that would make it certain, that is, a supernatural effect by which God would testify or declare that what was said was true, as is plain in Gedeon[[Judg 6:17||]], Ezechias[[4 Kings 20:8||]] and many others. But Zachary said this doubting, because he looked not to the omnipotence of God but to the course of nature, and to the natural order and causality, as the following words show: [[1:18|For I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in years|Ego enim sum senex, et uxor mea processit in diebus suis]]: as if to say, We are barren through old age. Zachary does not seem to have been in doubt about what kind of angel it was, whether a good spirit or an evil one: on the contrary, he knew that it was an angel of light, because it appeared in a holy place and during divine worship, and announced things so wholesome, touching the honour of God and the salvation of all; and he gathered this same thing from the angel's manner of speaking and of comforting him. Since, then, he knew these things, it was blameworthy that, disbelieving, he asked for a sign: so he is rebuked and punished, yet most tenderly.

paras.t: Et respondens angelus, dixit ei: Ego sum Gabriel, de quo in Daniele legisti, quam fidelis sim populi tui adjutor: idcirco de veritate verborum meorum ambigere non debebas; qui adsto ante Deum, id est, vultui Dei incessanter intendo, et quorsum versus processero, a beatifica Divinitatis contemplatione nusquam avertor, neque recedo: ideo adsto ante Deum, tanquam ad obediendum paratus, atque in bono immobiliter confirmatus, et invariabili Deo stabiliter inavertibiliterque intentus: propterea mentiri non valeo. Hoc modo omnes angeli sancti Deo adstare dicuntur. Interdum vero Adstare sive Adsistere, strictius sumitur, prout egressionem seu emissionem ad exteriora officia seu ad viatores excludit. Sicque superiorum ordinum angeli Deo adsistere, inferiorum ministrare dicuntur, juxta illud Danielis: Millia millium ministrabant ei, et decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei. Sumendo autem Adstare primo modo, etiam apud Tobiam angelus quidam fatetur: Ego sum (inquiens) Raphael angelus, unus ex septem qui adstamus ante Deum. In Apocalypsi habetur: Gratia vobis et pax a Deo, et a septem spiritibus qui in conspectu throni ejus sunt. Sic demum scriptum est in Job, Factum est quum quadam die venissent filii Dei ut adsisterent coram Domino: quod ibi de inferioribus angelis dicitur.
paras.en: [[1:19|And the angel answering, said to him: I am Gabriel|Et respondens angelus, dixit ei: Ego sum Gabriel]], of whom thou hast read in Daniel[[Dan 10:13||]][[Dan 10:20||]] [the margin gives Dan. x, 13, 20, where the angel who strives for Daniel's people is taken to be Gabriel, who is named at Dan 8:16 and 9:21] how faithful a helper of thy people I am: therefore thou oughtest not to have doubted the truth of my words; [[1:19|who stand before God|qui adsto ante Deum]], that is, I look unceasingly upon the face of God, and whithersoever I go forth, I am never turned away from the beatific contemplation of the Godhead, nor do I withdraw from it: so I stand before God as one ready to obey, immovably confirmed in good, and steadfastly and unswervingly intent upon the unchanging God; therefore I cannot lie. In this way all the holy angels are said to stand before God. But sometimes "to stand before" or "to assist" is taken more strictly, so as to exclude going out, or being sent out, to outward offices or to wayfarers [that is, men still on their pilgrimage in this life]. And so the angels of the higher orders are said to assist God, and those of the lower orders to minister, according to that of Daniel: [[Dan 7:10|thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times a hundred thousand stood before him|Millia millium ministrabant ei, et decies millies centena millia adsistebant ei]]. And taking "to stand before" in the first sense, an angel in Tobias too declares: [[Tob 12:15|I am the angel Raphael, one of the seven, who stand before the Lord|Ego sum (inquiens) Raphael angelus, unus ex septem qui adstamus ante Deum]]. In the Apocalypse we read: [[Apoc 1:4|Grace be unto you and peace|Gratia vobis et pax]] from God, and [[Apoc 1:4|from the seven spirits which are before his throne|a septem spiritibus qui in conspectu throni ejus sunt]]. So, lastly, it is written in Job: It came to pass, [[Job 1:6|on a certain day, when the sons of God came to stand before the Lord|quum quadam die venissent filii Dei ut adsisterent coram Domino]][[Job 2:1||]]: which is said there of the lower angels.

paras.t: Et missus sum loqui ad te, et, pro id est, hæc tibi evangelizare: quod est bonum quid annuntiare. Itaque, si missus fuit a Deo, stetitque realiter coram Zacharia in templo, quomodo pro eodem tempore fuit adstans ante Deum? Qui enim adstat ante Deum, videtur esse in cœlo: angelus autem in pluribus locis simul esse non potest. Et respondendum, quod Deus tanquam immensus ubique est: unde ut mens creata ei adsistat seu adstet, non oportet quod ipsa in cœlo sit; imo quocumque vadat, veniat vel exsistat, intra incircumscriptibilem Deum manet, cui omnis ille adstare asseritur, qui ei prompte obsequitur, aut contemplando infigitur. Contemplatio autem certum non exigit locum. Hinc ait Psalmista: Mane adstabo tibi et videbo.
paras.en: [[1:19|and am sent to speak to thee|Et missus sum loqui ad te]], and (standing for "that is") [[1:19|to bring thee these good tidings|hæc tibi evangelizare]], which is to announce something good. So, if he was sent by God and stood really before Zachary in the temple, how was he at the same time standing before God? For he who stands before God seems to be in heaven, and an angel cannot be in several places at once. And the answer is that God, being immense, is everywhere: so that for a created mind to assist or stand before Him, it need not be in heaven; rather, wherever it goes, comes or is, it remains within the uncircumscribable God, before whom everyone is said to stand who readily obeys Him, or is fixed upon Him in contemplation. And contemplation requires no fixed place. Hence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 5:5|In the morning I will stand before thee, and I will see|Mane adstabo tibi et videbo]].

paras.t: Et ecce. Per hanc vocem, Ecce, adverbialiter, demonstratur aut insinuatur notabile esse quod dicitur seu monstratur. Eris tacens, ita quod usu loquendi carebis, et non poteris loqui, quia et facultatem loquendi amittes. Eratque facile angelo instrumenta loquelæ taliter immutare, quod verba formari non poterant, sicut in Genesi legitur, angelum tetigisse nervum Jacob, qui protinus claudicavit. Usque in diem quo hæc fient, id est usque ad diem nativitatis, vel potius circumcisionis pueri, quando vocatum est nomen ejus Joannes, ut dixerat angelus. Non enim Zacharias loquelam recepit ante diem circumcisionis Joannis, ut infra describitur. Itaque angelus Deo sibi inspirante, dedit Zachariæ signum ut petiit, sed non tale quale optavit: et juste atque utiliter signum pœnale ac instructivum ad fidem sumit in subtractione loquelæ, ut qui discredendo fuit locutus, tacendo disceret esse verbis cœlestibus credulus. Nempe, ut ait Chrysostomus, dum Deus aliquid indicat, oportet illud in fide suscipere: nam super hujuscemodi disceptare, contumacis est animæ. Itaque signum istud in quantum fuit pœnale, datum est Zachariæ in pœnam suæ incredulitatis, ut subditur: pro eo quod non credidisti verbis meis, quæ implebuntur in tempore suo, id est tempore congruo, divinitusque præfixo, juxta illud Sapientis: Omnia tempus habent, et suis spatiis transeunt universa sub sole. Verumtamen putandum non est, quod Zacharias putaverit verba angeli esse falsa; nec penitus fuit incredulus, sed partim discredens atque ambiguus, nimis convertendo se ad naturalium cursum ordinemque causarum, non ad considerationem omnipotentiæ Dei, et certitudinem nuntii.
paras.en: [[1:20|And behold|Et ecce]]. By this word, Behold, used as an adverb, it is shown or hinted that what is said or pointed out is worthy of note. [[1:20|thou shalt be dumb|Eris tacens]], so that thou shalt lack the use of speech, [[1:20|and shalt not be able to speak|et non poteris loqui]], because thou shalt lose the very power of speaking. And it was easy for the angel so to alter the organs of speech that words could not be formed, as we read in Genesis that an angel touched the sinew of Jacob, who at once went lame[[Gen 32:25||]]. [[1:20|until the day wherein these things shall come to pass|Usque in diem quo hæc fient]], that is, until the day of the child's birth, or rather of his circumcision, when his name was called John, as the angel had said. For Zachary did not recover his speech before the day of John's circumcision, as is described below. So the angel, God inspiring him, gave Zachary a sign as he asked, but not such a one as he wished: and justly and profitably he receives the sign, one that both punishes him and instructs him in faith, in the taking away of his speech, so that he who had spoken in disbelief might learn by keeping silence to believe the words of heaven. For, as Chrysostom says, when God makes something known, it must be received in faith: for to dispute over such things belongs to a stubborn soul. So this sign, inasmuch as it was penal, was given to Zachary as a punishment for his unbelief, as is added: [[1:20|because thou hast not believed my words, which shall be fulfilled in their time|pro eo quod non credidisti verbis meis, quæ implebuntur in tempore suo]], that is, at the fitting time, fixed beforehand by God, according to that of the Wise man: [[Eccles 3:1|All things have their season, and in their times all things pass under heaven|Omnia tempus habent, et suis spatiis transeunt universa sub sole]]. Yet it is not to be thought that Zachary supposed the angel's words to be false; nor was he wholly unbelieving, but partly disbelieving and doubtful, turning too much to the course of natural things and the order of causes, and not to the consideration of God's omnipotence and the certainty of the messenger.

paras.t: Et erat plebs exspectans Zachariam: quia ut dictum est, foris mansit in atrio, nec Sancta ingredi potuit, neque recedere debuit, donec completo sacrificio, sacerdos qui pro ipsis oravit, egrederetur. Et mirabantur quod tardaret ipse in templo præter solitum. Non enim consuetum fuit tam diu insistere tali sacrificio, et causam dilationis ignoraverunt.
paras.en: [[1:21|And the people were waiting for Zachary|Et erat plebs exspectans Zachariam]]: because, as was said, they remained outside in the court, and could not enter the Holy Place, nor ought they to go away until the sacrifice was completed and the priest who prayed for them came out. [[1:21|and they wondered that he tarried so long in the temple|Et mirabantur quod tardaret ipse in templo]], beyond what was usual. For it was not the custom to spend so long over such a sacrifice, and they did not know the reason for the delay.

paras.t: Egressus autem de templo, et loco altaris incensi, non poterat loqui ad illos, et cognoverunt quod visionem vidisset, id est, cœlestem apparitionem seu angelicam revelationem habuisset, in templo. Hoc etenim consideraverunt ex mora præfata, et mirabili vultus sui alteratione ex colloquio angeli, ex amissione quoque loquelæ. Voluit enim Deus sciri a populo quod ei angelus apparuisset, quatenus postea cognita plenius veritate, et qualiter angelus nativitatem prænuntiasset Joannis, populus jam inciperet disponi ad fidem adventus Messiæ, quem et Zacharias iste utique prædicavit venisse. Unde et supersapientissimo Deo omnia optime moderante ac dispensante, permissus est Zacharias incredulitatem incidere; atque loquela privatus est, quatenus fama Joannis cordibus Judæorum tenacius ac celebrius infigeretur, sicque postea testimoniis ejus de Christo celerius crederent. Et ipse erat innuens illis, id est, visibili signo seu nutu indicavit eis, ut essent contenti atque abirent, et forte, quod aliquid sibi divinitus contigisset; et permansit mutus usque in diem circumcisionis Joannis. Ita et quilibet obmutescere debet, facta sibi revelatione superna, nec illam mox prodere, quousque Deus eam voluerit aliis pandi.
paras.en: [[1:22|And when he came out|Egressus autem]] of the temple and from the place of the altar of incense, [[1:22|he could not speak to them: and they understood that he had seen a vision|non poterat loqui ad illos, et cognoverunt quod visionem vidisset]], that is, that he had had a heavenly apparition or an angelic revelation, [[1:22|in the temple|in templo]]. For they gathered this from the delay just mentioned, and from the wonderful change in his countenance after speaking with the angel, and also from the loss of his speech. For God willed the people to know that an angel had appeared to him, so that afterwards, when the truth was more fully known, and how the angel had foretold the birth of John, the people might begin even then to be disposed to faith in the coming of the Messias, whom this Zachary too certainly preached to have come. Hence also, God in His supreme wisdom ruling and ordering all things for the best[[Wis 8:1||]][[Wis 12:15||]], Zachary was allowed to fall into unbelief, and was deprived of speech, so that the fame of John might be fixed more firmly and more widely in the hearts of the Jews, and so that afterwards they might the more readily believe his testimony of Christ. [[1:22|And he made signs to them|Et ipse erat innuens illis]], that is, he showed them by a visible sign or nod that they should be content and go away, and perhaps that something had happened to him from God; [[1:22|and remained dumb|et permansit mutus]] until the day of John's circumcision. So too everyone ought to keep silent when a revelation from above has been made to him, and not betray it at once, until God wills it to be disclosed to others.

paras.t: Et factum est, ut impleti sunt dies officii sui, id est completa hebdomada qua ministravit in templo, infra quam mansit, ut dictum est, circa templum, abiit in domum suam, quæ, ut legitur, non fuit in civitate Jerusalem, sed in alia quadam. Quum ergo sacerdotes veteris legis, quorum sacerdotium vile, carnale, ac typicum fuit, respectu sacerdotii Christi seu evangelicæ legis, ita ab ingressu propriarum domorum, ab accessu quoque legitimarum abstinuerint conjugum, atque circa templum manentes, puritati ac devotioni ita vacaverint tempore sui officii, quam damnabiles et scelerati sunt sacerdotes jam Christi, qui vel quotidie vel frequenter sacramenta Christi contrectant, aliisque ministrant et celebrant, et tamen carnalibus vitiis inquinantur, et non suis miscentur!
paras.en: [[1:23|And it came to pass, after the days of his office were accomplished|Et factum est, ut impleti sunt dies officii sui]], that is, when the week was completed in which he ministered in the temple, during which, as was said, he stayed about the temple, [[1:23|he departed to his own house|abiit in domum suam]], which, as we read, was not in the city of Jerusalem but in another town. Since, then, the priests of the old law, whose priesthood was mean, carnal and figurative in comparison with the priesthood of Christ, or of the Gospel law, kept away from entering their own houses and from approaching their lawful wives, and, staying about the temple, gave themselves so to purity and devotion in the time of their office, how damnable and wicked are those who are now priests of Christ, who handle the sacraments of Christ daily or often, and minister them to others and celebrate, and yet are defiled with carnal vices, and have to do with women who are not their own!

paras.t: Post hos autem dies, scilicet Zacharia in domum suam reverso, concepit Elisabeth uxor ejus: quæ vel per revelationem supernam, vel per signa mariti, vel aliorum relatu cognovit, quod vir suus visionem vidisset, et non ex carnalis voluptatis amore aut propria motione, sed desiderio prolis, et ex inspiratione divina, eam in tanta senectute accederet: idcirco reniti non debuit. Concepit autem, secundum expositores, mense Septembri, octavo calendas Octobris, luna undecima, in æquinoctio autumnali.
paras.en: [[1:24|And after those days|Post hos autem dies]], that is, after Zachary had returned to his house, [[1:24|Elizabeth his wife conceived|concepit Elisabeth uxor ejus]]: she knew, whether by a revelation from above, or by her husband's signs, or from what others told her, that her husband had seen a vision, and that it was not from love of carnal pleasure or by his own impulse, but from desire of offspring and by divine inspiration, that he came to her in so great an old age: and so she ought not to resist. And she conceived, according to the commentators, in the month of September, on the eighth day before the Kalends of October [that is, 24 September], on the eleventh day of the moon, at the autumn equinox.

paras.t: Et occultabat se mensibus quinque, dicens: Quia sic fecit mihi Dominus, id est, fecunditatem hanc supernaturaliter mihi donavit, in diebus senii mei, quibus respexit, id est, suo pio, omnipotenti, causalissimoque respectu dignatus est auferre opprobrium meum inter homines, id est confusionem quæ mihi ab hominibus imminebat, eo quod sterilis essem. Sterilitas quippe in lege maledictioni subjacuit: non quod infecundi essent apud Dominum maledicti, quum nec Elias nec Jeremias viri sanctissimi duxerint conjuges; sed maledictio illa fuit quoddam humanum opprobrium, quoniam pudor fuit conjugatis, nuptiarum fructu carere. Imo Ambrosius ait: Pudor est feminis nuptiarum præmia non habere, quibus hæc sola est causa nubendi. Hoc tamen pro tempore gratiæ ita intelligendum non est, quasi non sit conjugatis magis meritorium amore Dei et castitatis penitus continere, quam proles generare, sed quia homines reputant inhonestum in matrimonio prolem non procreare. Apud Deum vero quædam sterilitas felix asseritur, juxta illud Sapientis: Felix sterilis et incoinquinata, quæ nescivit torum in delicto.
paras.en: [[1:24|and hid herself five months, saying|Et occultabat se mensibus quinque, dicens]]: [[1:25|Thus hath the Lord dealt with me|Quia sic fecit mihi Dominus]], that is, He has given me this fruitfulness above nature, [[1:25|in the days|in diebus]] of my old age, [[1:25|wherein he hath had regard|quibus respexit]], that is, by His loving, almighty and all-causing regard He has deigned [[1:25|to take away my reproach among men|auferre opprobrium meum inter homines]], that is, the shame that threatened me from men, because I was barren. For barrenness lay under a curse in the Law[[Deut 7:14||]]: not that the childless were accursed before the Lord, since neither Elias nor Jeremias, most holy men, took wives; but that curse was a kind of human reproach, since it was a shame for married people to lack the fruit of marriage. Indeed Ambrose says: It is a shame for women not to have the rewards of marriage, for whom this is the only reason for marrying. Yet for the time of grace this is not to be understood as though it were not more meritorious for married people to abstain altogether for the love of God and of chastity than to beget children, but in the sense that men think it unseemly not to have children in marriage. But with God a certain barrenness is called happy, according to that of the Wise man: [[Wis 3:13|happy is the barren: and the undefiled, that hath not known bed in sin|Felix sterilis et incoinquinata, quæ nescivit torum in delicto]].

paras.t: Denique, quamvis sancta Elisabeth læta sit valde de conceptione filii tam illustris, et quod supernaturaliter fecunda effecta est, itemque, quia consideravit quod filius nasciturus esset magnæ perfectionis futurus, et quia a nota sterilitatis fuerat liberata; erubuit tamen, quod in senectute sua acciderit istud, quando de lege communi non est tempus commixtionis, prout in Ecclesiaste scriptum est: Tempus amplectendi, et tempus longe fieri ab amplexibus. Sic et Sara ait in Genesi: Postquam consenui, et dominus meus vetulus est, voluptati operam dabo? tanquam diceret, Indecens est. Verum divina voluntas nulla lege præstringitur, nullo ordine coarctatur, sed omnis legis et ordinis causa supertranscendit: ideo quidquid jusserit, bonum, justum, et decens est, quocumque tempore id agi mandaverit. Itaque ex pudore seu erubescentia occultavit se Elisabeth mensibus quinque, scilicet donec beatissima virgo Maria conciperet, et proles Elisabeth exsultans in gaudio prophetaret, ut Origenes exponit.
paras.en: Lastly, although holy Elizabeth rejoiced greatly at the conception of so illustrious a son, and that she had been made fruitful above nature, and also because she considered that the son to be born would be of great perfection, and because she had been freed from the stigma of barrenness, yet she blushed that this had happened in her old age, when by the common law it is not the time for intercourse, as it is written in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 3:5|A time to embrace, and a time to be far from embraces|Tempus amplectendi, et tempus longe fieri ab amplexibus]]. So too Sara says in Genesis: [[Gen 18:12|After I am grown old, and my lord is an old man, shall I give myself to pleasure?|Postquam consenui, et dominus meus vetulus est, voluptati operam dabo?]] as if to say, It is unseemly. But the divine will is bound by no law and confined by no order; being the cause of every law and order, it transcends them all: so whatever it commands is good, just and seemly, at whatever time it bids it be done.
